claim: Balance is the distribution of visual weight, and it is what an author actually means when they say a frame feels wrong but cannot say why. Symmetrical is formal and inhuman, weighted_top crushes the subject, chaotic is what a frame looks like when nothing is under control.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: subject on the left, empty space on the right
subject on the right, empty space on the left
visual weight at the bottom, heavy lower frame, empty upper frame
visual weight at the top, heavy upper frame, empty lower frame
diagonal composition, elements arranged along a diagonal
radial composition, elements radiating from the center

review.issue: weighted_bottom, weighted_top and radial are written in critic's language, not tags — "visual weight at the bottom", "heavy lower frame", "empty upper frame" have no danbooru counterpart and will read as baseline. asym_left/asym_right restate thirds_bias.left_third/right_third and hit the left/right gap. symmetrical duplicates thirds_bias.symmetrical, and radial ("radial composition, elements radiating from the center") duplicates comp.leading_lines.radial ("radial lines, lines radiating from the center") almost word for word.
review.fix: Delete the values other cards already own (asym_*, symmetrical, radial) and express the weighting values as content the model can actually draw — e.g. weighted_top as "towering structure above, small figure below", weighted_bottom as "low horizon, open sky above" — or drop them. What is left that is genuinely this card's own is diagonal and chaotic.

look_at: asym_left/right and chaotic read; weighted_top/bottom do not.
